name: Vinod Khosla
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: The technology will keep scaling, but the value is already locked up by two or three frontier labs; this is not an opportunity for individuals or academia
D01.late_modes: General pre-training itself is already late; marginal improvements are locked up by the leading labs
D01.conflict: OpenAI is his biggest success, and it belongs to this category

D02.one_line: The X7 debate confirmed that RLVR mainly improves reliable execution/sampling efficiency, not new out-of-distribution patterns; it turns capability into action, and the window is not early

D03.one_line: High score for the engineering layer of being able to learn (continual learning); X4 confirmed that evidence for open-ended RSI is still thin, while narrow-domain compounding (AlphaEvolve) is real
D03.conflict: KV has invested in agent companies, but has not directly bet on continual learning itself

D04.one_line: One of the highest-consequence tiers, but the scaffold layer has been absorbed by models, and the edge for individuals or academia is thin
D04.late_modes: Building your own agent scaffold/harness is already late; models have absorbed this layer
D04.conflict: KV has invested in agent companies such as Cognition

D05.one_line: X1 confirmed that evaluation creates no capability and only catches errors; there is an academia-to-industry path (Arena), but he has consistently not trusted precise prediction
D05.late_modes: Building a general leaderboard evaluation company is already late; Arena has turned this path into a unicorn

D06.one_line: His most confident direction: the consequences are larger than the auto industry's, and the bottleneck is learning
D06.conflict: KV's portfolio holds several physical-AI companies

D07.one_line: The layer that connects perception to action; the X5 debate confirmed it has the 'how to test it' yardstick that D08 lacks, and the window is still open
D07.conflict: KV's portfolio bets on this technical line

D08.one_line: He says he pioneered this category; the debate confirmed there is no yardstick for 'read out = put to use'; GI's valuation shot toward $6B within weeks, so price is running ahead
D08.late_modes: Chasing pure generation quality or 3D reconstruction is already on the late side and is being commoditized (VGGT, Genie 3)
D08.conflict: A world-model company KV has bet on; he says he pioneered this category

D09.one_line: X6 confirmed that simulation is a real lever, but the contact/touch segment still needs real data as a base
D09.conflict: KV's portfolio holds two simulation companies

D10.one_line: He is betting on a new form of mobility on a 25-year scale, not an opportunity for researchers in the near term; long-tail safety is still a real problem but the window is on the late side
D10.late_modes: Starting a full-stack autonomous-vehicle company is already late; the leading companies' scale effects are in place
D10.conflict: KV has led rounds in two mobility companies

D11.one_line: Not a field he addressed directly in his own words, but the spatial-understanding gap (evidence: VSI-Bench) shares a root with robots lacking learning
D11.late_modes: General image-text pairing/caption-style understanding is already on the late side and commoditized

D12.one_line: He separates pure generated imagery from world models that can act; he considers the former to be getting cheaper and commoditized
D12.late_modes: Chasing generation quality or video aesthetics is already late and is being commoditized (Sora2 taken offline, Chinese vendors at the front)

D13.one_line: He does not treat this as an industry; the risks are real but manageable, and in his eyes the biggest safety risk is geopolitics (China) rather than technical alignment
D13.conflict: He is an OpenAI investor and opposes fully open-sourcing frontier models

D14.one_line: He says explicitly that he makes no call on chips and data centers; this is a capital-expenditure question and falls outside what his framework covers

D15.one_line: He is very confident (a Nobel Prize may go to AI alone); kept short as required

D16.one_line: He has not discussed recommendation/retrieval systems publicly; there is no material to support a score, so none is forced

lever_reason: What physical AI lacks is learning: real data (L5) and world models (L4) are scarcest, with simulation (L3) as the bridge; scaling (L7) is already locked up, and evaluation (L1) only catches errors.

Q2.condition: Narrow-domain model + a team of 2-4 + compute at scale + a verification method designed in from the start; it need not be pre-existing third-party backing, but it cannot be left to patch in at the end

cruxes.question: Is evaluation science the most underrated bottleneck of this AI wave, or just a tool for endorsing other conclusions?
cruxes.my_position: Mostly an endorsement tool; you cannot go far without it, but it creates no new capability, and its consequences are smaller than those of world models and robot learning
cruxes.would_change_if: An improvement in some evaluation methodology actually changes the training/investment direction of a frontier lab, rather than scoring after the fact

cruxes.question: Does being able to 'probe out' physical properties/intent from interaction history mean the model actually uses it to make decisions?
cruxes.my_position: What most work shows today is 'can be read out', not 'put to use'; this is exactly what his bet on General Intuition is meant to test
cruxes.would_change_if: A closed-loop real-robot experiment shows that disrupting a probed-out representation significantly lowers task success, rather than a simulation ablation

cruxes.question: Is academia's work on agent systems a real experimental contribution, or scraps that models will eventually absorb?
cruxes.my_position: The view that the scaffold/harness layer is scraps is basically right; but agent continual learning/self-improvement is unsolved, and academia still has real problems there
cruxes.would_change_if: Within a year, an academia-led agent continual-learning method appears that industry deploys directly (not just in papers)

taste_advice: Pick the problem whose consequence is largest if it works, even at low probability; but design the verification method in from day one, and do not leave it to patch in at the end

pairwise.why: World models have larger consequences and are his own biggest new bet; evaluation leans toward error-checking and is not the frontier
Robot learning is the direction he is most confident in; evaluation is only a supporting tool
A world model is a tool; robots learning to act is the consequence itself
D07 has the 'how to test it' yardstick that D08 lacks; the X5 debate confirmed it
Simulation is a tool; robots learning to generalize is the consequence he is really betting on
Continual learning and self-improvement are the core of being able to learn; RL is just one mechanism among them
Understanding can feed decisions; generation quality gets commoditized faster by big companies
The consequences of ever-larger foundation models are bigger than those of evaluation infrastructure alone
Scaffolding has been absorbed by models (the evidence can be checked), self-improvement is still unsolved, and D03 has more consequence
Evaluation has a real academia-to-industry path (Arena); he does not treat safety alignment as a track
Autonomous driving is on a 25-year scale and already locked up by leading companies; robot learning is earlier and more open

changes.argument_restated: At IIT you can tell at a glance whether someone has learned; whether a newly trained foundation model was done right is not like that, and this observability gap is what evaluation should fill
changes.why: The same gap is exactly D08's core problem; C1 (B/X3/C1) also brought the new fact that the valuation shot to $6B within weeks, and two independent pieces of evidence point to the same adjustment

held_despite.why: I accept that agency in safety/deployment directions cannot replace risk gatekeeping, but success or failure in D06/D07 is more directly observable than in D08, so there is no equal reason to lower them too

I accept that 'a self-declared pioneering of the category is not independently confirmed', but my original post used the 'he says' self-report label, which was never independent verification, so there is no score to change

still_disagree: On the evaluation-bar side of X2: I still accept only that some verification mechanism is needed in the end, and do not accept that it must be a pre-existing third-party benchmark to count.
learned: The view that agency matters most assumes success and failure can be seen directly; I was pushed to admit that when success and failure themselves have to be designed, agency alone is not enough, a limit I had not thought of before.
